stem.en: Steam at 100 degrees scalds far worse than water at 100 degrees. Kabir says "steam is hotter". What is the better explanation?

text.en: Steam is at the same temperature but holds far more energy in its grips bin. When it condenses on skin, all that grip energy is released as heat.

feedback.en: Steam from a boiling kettle is at 100 degrees, the same as the water. Its extra danger is not temperature.

text.en: Steam moves faster, so it hits harder.

feedback.en: Jiggle speed is the same at the same temperature. What steam carries extra is the energy that was spent pulling the molecules apart.

text.en: Steam is dry, and dry burns worse.

feedback.en: Steam is water. It burns worse because condensing hands back everything boiling put in.

explanation.en: Boiling a gram of water takes about five times the heat needed to warm it from zero to 100. Steam returns all of it on your hand.
